title: Designing Human-in-the-Loop Review and Approval Gates for AI Workflows (2026)

questions.question: Which output description is classified as CRITICAL by classify_risk?
options: An internal reversible meeting summary with no downstream action
A reversible customer notification draft awaiting a send decision
A safety-facing recommendation, even before considering model confidence
A reversible internal data lookup with no recipient
questions.explanation: The classifier treats audience='safety' or downstream_action='safety_system' as CRITICAL. The gate is driven by consequence and reversibility, not by a confidence percentage.

questions.question: What tier does OUT-002, a reversible customer-facing renewal draft, receive?
options: Tier 1 LOW, because the draft has not been sent
Tier 3 HIGH, because every customer message is irreversible
Tier 4 CRITICAL, because renewal notices are financial by definition
Tier 2 MEDIUM, because customer-facing output requires an asynchronous review
questions.explanation: classify_risk checks audience after critical and high-impact branches. A reversible customer output is MEDIUM, which carries the 30-second review-hold policy.

questions.question: Why is OUT-004 classified HIGH and still flagged as a rubber stamp?
options: It is irreversible and financial, so it is Tier 3; the 8-second acceptance is below the 60-second hold
It is LOW because customer outputs are reversible, so no flag should appear
It is CRITICAL because every financial output needs two reviewers
It is MEDIUM because the primary reviewer accepted the recommendation
questions.explanation: An irreversible financial output maps to RiskTier.HIGH. is_rubber_stamp compares its 8-second acceptance with the HIGH hold of 60 seconds and flags the event.

questions.question: What final event does run_gate append for OUT-005 after both primary and secondary reviewers escalate?
options: ACCEPT by the primary reviewer, because escalation is treated as approval
HOLD by decision_owner (timeout -> conservative default)
REJECT by the senior reviewer, because any second escalation is a rejection
REVISE by the decision owner, because the conservative default edits the output
questions.explanation: After two ESCALATE events, run_gate exhausts ESCALATION_CHAIN and appends a decision_owner event with CONSERVATIVE_DEFAULT, which is HOLD.

questions.question: Which event does is_rubber_stamp flag in the synthetic batch?
options: OUT-002, accepted in 95 seconds against the MEDIUM tier's 30-second minimum
OUT-001, accepted immediately even though LOW has no hold requirement
OUT-004, accepted in 8 seconds against the HIGH tier's 60-second minimum
OUT-005, because a HOLD after escalation is faster than 120 seconds
questions.explanation: Only an ACCEPT faster than the tier hold is a rubber-stamp event. OUT-004 is 8<60; OUT-001 is exempt as LOW, OUT-002 exceeds 30 seconds, and OUT-005 is HOLD.

questions.question: Why is OUT-002 not flagged even though its review is asynchronous?
options: Customer-facing drafts never enter the gate
The reviewer accepted it before the hold timer started
The MEDIUM tier has no timing policy when the output is reversible
Its 95-second acceptance exceeds the MEDIUM tier's 30-second minimum
questions.explanation: MEDIUM outputs have a 30-second hold, and OUT-002 took 95 seconds. Its async review is valid and does not trigger is_rubber_stamp.
